title: A Method for the Calculation of the Zeta-Function
venue: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (2) 48, 180–197
source_edition: King’s College Turing Digital Archive original offprint
audit_scope: The archive offprint prints 1943 on p. 180 and received/read dates in March 1939. The publisher DOI landing page uses 1945. Method and error estimates were sampled. No finite zero census is claimed from this item.

main_results.statement: Article derives a zeta evaluation method from an approximate functional equation with an integral remainder. The proposed approximation replaces the remainder integral by a finite sum and adjusts the main sums. The author identifies the intermediate range between small-height Euler–Maclaurin evaluation and the large-height Riemann–Siegel regime as the primary use case.

local_version_receipt: Original viewed and checksummed. Archive scan excluded from the retained source folder.

title: Some Calculations of the Riemann Zeta-Function
venue: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society (3) 3(1), 99–117
source_edition: King’s College Turing Digital Archive original offprint
audit_scope: Historical claim read with its own caveat. Lehman's later correction to details is cited by Trudgian and Saouter–Gourdon–Demichel. This is neither a modern interval-arithmetic replay nor a verified initial segment extending to the high band.

main_results.statement: The paper uses an explicit integrated argument estimate and a zero-counting criterion for the Manchester Mark 1 computation. The primary run reports simple critical-line zeros in the band 2π·63² < Im(s) < 2π·64², with the author's qualification on reliability. The smaller-height run was curtailed by breakdown.

title: A Method for Proving the Completeness of a List of Zeros of Certain L-Functions
audit_scope: The sufficiency direction in Theorem 3.2 has no RH assumption. The short proof of the converse accuracy/padding statement in that theorem invokes RH for the L-function. No numerical list was certified here.

main_results.statement: For the paper's L-function class, the smoothed Weil–Barner explicit-formula residual bounded above by 0.49 in (3.3), with the stated smoothing and interval conditions, certifies that the supplied critical-line list contains all nontrivial zeros with ordinates in [a,b]. The introduction compares asymptotic endpoint padding of O(log a log log a) and O(log b log log b) with the Turing procedure.

title: Isolating Some Non-Trivial Zeros of Zeta
source_edition: Bristol Research Portal accepted manuscript with institutional coversheet
audit_scope: Downloaded Bristol accepted manuscript with institutional coversheet. This source describes both rigorous isolation and completeness within its fixed range. The computation was not rerun.

main_results.statement: Reports isolation of every nontrivial zeta zero with positive ordinate ≤30,610,046,000 on the critical line to absolute precision ±2⁻¹⁰². Newton guesses are followed by certified opposite signs. The implementation uses MPFI at 300-bit working precision, explicit truncation bounds, and Turing completeness.

title: Numerical Computations Concerning the GRH
audit_scope: Scope involves both conductor and ordinate restrictions. Do not confuse parity of the modulus in the bound with parity of a character in the completed-function formula.

main_results.statement: Reports verification for primitive Dirichlet characters with q≤400,000. The height is max(10⁸/q, 7.5·10⁷/q+200) for even q and max(10⁸/q, 3.75·10⁷/q+200) for odd q, where parity here is that of the modulus.

title: Arb: Efficient Arbitrary-Precision Midpoint-Radius Interval Arithmetic
audit_scope: Enclosures certify individual numerical claims when mathematical remainder bounds and algorithm invariants also hold. The software paper supplies no completeness theorem for zeta zeros.

main_results.statement: Arb represents real enclosures by midpoint and radius, propagates error bounds in arbitrary-precision operations, and supports real/complex special functions. This is the interval infrastructure that Platt–Trudgian name in their later finite-height count.

title: Rigorous High-Precision Computation of the Hurwitz Zeta Function and Its Derivatives
audit_scope: The pole at s=1 requires the paper's deflation/continuation treatment for evaluation. Finite positive Li values do not prove the all-index criterion.

main_results.statement: A coefficientwise computable Euler–Maclaurin remainder bound applies to the formal Taylor series ζ(s+x,a) when positive integers N,M satisfy Re(a)+N>1 and Re(s)+2M>1. It supports arbitrary-order derivative enclosures and a worked finite Li-coefficient application.

title: Fast Methods to Compute the Riemann Zeta Function
source_edition: primary journal, conference, or author-hosted working copy
audit_scope: Journal PDF checked. This is a complexity bound for evaluation including precomputation, not a zero count or a single asymptotic runtime guarantee for an implementation.

main_results.statement: For fixed accuracy exponent λ and t>1, computes ζ(1/2+it) to absolute error t⁻λ with t^(4/13) times polylogarithmic arithmetic operations on Oλ((log t)²)-bit numbers. Precomputation and storage have their own t^(4/13) times polylogarithmic costs.

title: Fast Algorithms for Multiple Evaluations of the Riemann Zeta Function
venue: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society 309(2), 797–809
source_edition: primary journal, conference, or author-hosted working copy
audit_scope: The end-to-end zero-verification cost is phrased as expected in the source. The timetable does not certify which values are zeros or that a sign-change list is complete.

main_results.statement: After O(T^(1/2+ε)) precomputation and a comparable storage bound, the algorithm can evaluate ζ(σ+it) at fixed σ and T≤t≤T+T^(1/2) to polynomially small error using O(T^ε) operations per value. The paper describes expected near-linear costs for initial zero verification.

title: The Zeta Function on the Critical Line: Numerical Evidence for Moments and Random Matrix Theory Models
audit_scope: Author-hosted 31-page preprint is the accessed copy. Finite-window variation is an empirical finding and does not establish or refute the asymptotic moment formulas.

main_results.statement: Reports noticeable variation of high empirical moments even across intervals containing roughly 10⁹ zeros near zero number 10²³. Compares computed integral moments with random-matrix-informed predictions and describes numerical trends for shifted/adjacent statistics.

title: Lehmer Pairs of Zeros, the de Bruijn–Newman Constant Λ, and the Riemann Hypothesis
source_edition: primary journal, conference, or author-hosted working copy
audit_scope: The finite computation is an application of a global heat-flow comparison theorem. The sharp Lehmer-pair condition involves surrounding zeros, not an absolute gap threshold alone.

main_results.statement: Defines a Lehmer pair via its small gap relative to the inverse-square contribution from other zeros and derives a corresponding lower bound for Λ. The applied bound in Theorem 3 is −4.379·10⁻⁶ < Λ.

title: A New Lehmer Pair of Zeros and a New Lower Bound for the de Bruijn–Newman Constant Λ
audit_scope: Author-hosted copy explicitly records correction on 29 June 1994. The 1993 journal identity is retained, and the corrected version is the one inspected.

main_results.locator: Corrected edition, p. 104 abstract and numerical sections
main_results.statement: Reports −5.895·10⁻⁹ < Λ from a very close pair of consecutive zeros using rigorous control of the inverse-square remainder in the Lehmer criterion.

title: An Improved Bound for the de Bruijn–Newman Constant
audit_scope: An individual pair/location result is different from certifying all zeros below the pair's ordinate. The negative lower bound has been superseded.

main_results.locator: Author manuscript abstract and early sections
main_results.statement: Gives Λ>−2.7·10⁻⁹ from a close pair of consecutive zeta zeros near zero index 10²⁰. The result uses the Lehmer-pair criterion, so checking a short relevant block can improve a global lower bound.

title: An Improved Lower Bound for the de Bruijn–Newman Constant
source_edition: primary journal, conference, or author-hosted working copy
audit_scope: All seven printed pages were read. MPFR/Riemann–Siegel computation and quoted global inequalities were not replayed. Table 3's GUE-based probabilities are heuristic and separate from the lower-bound argument.

main_results.statement: Reports Λ>−1.14541·10⁻¹¹. Independently checks local zero isolation and completeness for a close pair near ordinate 7.954022502373·10¹², derives G_K≤379.1995 and gap squared times G_K≤3.47471·10⁻⁸, and invokes the Lehmer criterion. For the negative lower bound, failure of RH or existence of a multiple zero yields the inequality directly by the cited theory.

title: Effective Approximation of Heat Flow Evolution of the Riemann ξ Function, and a New Upper Bound for the de Bruijn–Newman Constant
venue: Research in the Mathematical Sciences 6, article 31
audit_scope: Additional stronger table values in §10 require specified higher initial verification. The separate already-recorded Platt–Trudgian paper invokes the 0.2 row once the required height is verified.

main_results.statement: Proves Λ≤0.22 by combining finite t=0 zero information through X/2, an asymptotic zero-free statement at t₀, and a certified barrier through intermediate times. The stated choices are t₀=y₀=0.2 and X=6·10¹⁰+83952−0.5, so the theorem yields t₀+y₀²/2=0.22.

title: Accurate Estimation of Sums over Zeros of the Riemann Zeta-Function
audit_scope: The sum is over all zero ordinates with the paper's endpoint convention. This scalar smooth-weight estimation does not give a general positive residual operator for a finite compression.

main_results.statement: For a nonnegative C² function φ with φ′≤0 and φ″≥0, 2π≤T₀≤T, and a finite integral ∫_T^∞ φ(t) log(t/(2π))dt, the half-endpoint ordinate tail minus that integral divided by 2π equals −φ(T)Q(T)+E₂(T), where E₂(T)=−∫_T^∞φ′(t)Q(t)dt and Q=N−L. Equation (3) gives an explicit bound for E₂.
